title: The Summit: the judged final
summary: The sealed motion is argued for real with the side decided by a coin at the podium, the ballot is read aloud and the result announced either way, then the season book and the Sprout's second showcase.
materials: the motion card from the sealed envelope, opened at week 10
both case files from week 10, the one for and the one against
the sand timers, two minute and one minute, and the call bell
a judge: an adult who is not debating, in the room or on a call, whoever the family arranged
a printed ballot for the judge to write on, and a pen
this week's Sprout family audience card, for the teach-someone-younger quest

steps.title: The final: the coin, the clock and the ballot
steps.body:
The envelope sat on that shelf from week 1 and opened at week 10, and since then you have built two cases on the same motion, one for and one against, on purpose. Today a coin decides which one you get to use, thirty seconds before you speak.

That is why the app does not say which side you are on. The coin says.

The shape, three rounds, the format you have run since week 7. Round one, constructives, two minutes each: two points, each with a reason and a real piece of evidence, signposted so a listener always knows where you are, and one minute of cross-examination straight after each constructive. Round two, rebuttals, ninety seconds each, flow sheet open: answer their columns, not your notes. Round three, summaries, one minute each: collapse to the one argument you are actually winning and spend the whole minute there. No new arguments in a summary.

The clock is shared. It is the referee, not a punishment, and it has been that since week 1. When the bell goes you finish the sentence you are in and stop.

The judge is an adult who is not debating. They write on the ballot while you speak, they do not help either side, and when it is over they read the ballot out loud, in full, and announce the result. The result gets announced either way. A season that only reads the ballot when the ballot is kind has not learned anything about judges.

After the ballot, keep the camera up for two more things. The season book, five minutes: name it, say one thing it changed about how you think, describe one moment so a stranger could picture it, and say whether a friend should read it. Then three sentences, one per sprint, the moment from each that you would keep.

steps.title: Teach someone younger: produce their second showcase
steps.body:
At the end of last season they did their first showcase and you helped. This one is their second, and you are not the helper. You are the producer, which means everything except the performing.

Read the family audience card all the way through before anything else, so you know the four acts and their order: the counting, the take-away story, the pattern, and the seed. Then produce it. Set the room like it matters: family sitting as an audience, a spot on the floor where the star stands so everybody can see them, their cup with the sprout in it already on the table, their toys already counted out and waiting.

Then run the show. Introduce them, name each act before it starts so the audience knows what it is watching, and lead the applause after every one. One rule beats all the others: it is their show. They count at their speed, they clap their own pattern, they say what the seed needed. A wobble in the middle of the count is part of the act and not a problem to fix, and if they go shy, do the act beside them once and then hand it straight back.

Close it the card's way, by reading aloud to them in front of everybody, and let them sit where the audience can see their face rather than yours.

Watch for one thing they do that surprises you. You have watched them from the corner of your eye all season. Tonight you have the front row.
checklist: I read the family audience card all the way through before I set anything up
The room was set as a real audience, and they stood where everybody could see them
I named each act before it started and led the applause after every one
They did every act themselves, at their own speed, and I did not finish a single one for them
I read aloud to them to close the show, and noticed one thing they did that surprised me

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt:
Record the whole final: the coin flip, all three rounds, and the judge reading the ballot out loud with the result. Phone propped up, whole face in frame, no cuts and no second takes, whichever way it goes.

Then keep rolling for the five minutes on the season book, and then for your three sentences, one per sprint.

Last, one honest sentence with the camera still running: the strongest thing the other side said today, and what you would say back to it with another week to think.
